question: When a strict CoPP policy is implemented, which statement describes an event during which packets are dropped?
options: A large system image is copied to a switch by using the default VRF.
Fifteen SSH sessions remain connected to the switch.
A ping sweep is performed on a network that is connected through a switch.
A web server that is connected to a switch is affected by a DDoS attack.
theory: A strict CoPP policy applies the tightest committed-rate and burst (BC) values to every traffic class hitting the supervisor CPU. Bulk data transfers such as a large system-image copy sent through the default (non-management) VRF ride the in-band path that is subject to CoPP, so a large, sustained transfer easily exceeds the strict policy's conform rate and gets policed/dropped - unlike a modest number of SSH sessions, a normal ping sweep, or a DDoS aimed at a downstream server (not the switch's own control plane), none of which threaten to exceed the strict thresholds destined for the supervisor. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 18 - Nexus Control Plane Policing)
